bottom_line: In PIONEER AF-PCI, clinically significant bleeding was lower with rivaroxaban strategies than with vitamin K antagonist plus DAPT (group 1 vs. group 3 hazard ratio, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.47 to 0.76; group 2 vs. group 3 hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.80).
implications: These data support that, over 12 months, clinically significant bleeding occurred less often with rivaroxaban strategies (16.8% and 18.0%) than with vitamin K antagonist plus DAPT (26.7%), with hazard ratios vs standard therapy of 0.59 (95% CI, 0.47 to 0.76) and 0.63 (95% CI, 0.50 to 0.80). For efficacy, major adverse cardiovascular events were similar (6.5%, 5.6%, 6.0%), but the reported confidence intervals (e.g., 1.08 [0.69–1.68] and 0.93 [0.59–1.48]) and stated low power mean the results do not license firm conclusions regarding comparative efficacy.

major_points.text: International, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation undergoing PCI with stenting.
major_points.quote: PIONEER AF-PCI was an international, multi- center, randomized, open-label trial.

major_points.text: Randomized 2124 participants in a 1:1:1 ratio to two rivaroxaban-based strategies vs dose-adjusted vitamin K antagonist plus DAPT.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned 2124 participants with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation who had undergone PCI with stenting to receive, in a 1:1:1 ratio,

major_points.text: Group 2 regimen: rivaroxaban 2.5 mg twice daily plus DAPT (aspirin 75–100 mg/day plus a P2Y12 inhibitor) for 1, 6, or 12 months, with prespecified DAPT duration.
major_points.quote: Participants in group 2 were assigned to re- ceive rivaroxaban at a dose of 2.5 mg twice daily plus background DAPT with low-dose aspirin (75 to 100 mg per day) and clopidogrel

major_points.text: Primary safety endpoint was clinically significant bleeding (TIMI major/minor or bleeding requiring medical attention) during the treatment period.
major_points.quote: The primary safety end point was the occurrence of clinically significant bleeding (a composite of major bleeding or minor bleeding according to Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction [TIMI] criteria or bleeding requiring medical attention

major_points.text: Clinically significant bleeding at 12 months was lower in both rivaroxaban groups than in standard therapy, with hazard ratios vs group 3 of 0.59 and 0.63.
major_points.quote: At 12 months, the primary safety end point of clinically significant bleeding had occurred in 16.8% of participants in group 1, 18.0% in group 2, and 26.7% in group 3 (hazard ratio for group 1 vs. group 3, 0.59; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.47 to 0.76; P<0.001; hazard ratio for group 2 vs. group 3, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.80; P<0.001)

major_points.text: Secondary efficacy endpoint (death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke) had similar rates across groups, with wide confidence intervals.
major_points.quote: The rates of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke were similar in the three groups (Kaplan–Meier estimates, 6.5% in group 1, 5.6% in group 2, and 6.0% in group 3; P values for all comparisons were nonsignificant).

guidelines_referenced.text: European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Guidelines for the management of atrial fibrillation
guidelines_referenced.quote: Guidelines for the management of atrial fibrillation: the Task Force for the Man- agement of Atrial Fibrillation of the Euro- pean Society of Cardiology (ESC).

inclusion_criteria.text: Main inclusion criterion: documented atrial fibrillation within 1 year before screening; AF >1 year before screening eligible if receiving oral anticoagulation for AF for the 3 months immediately preceding the index PCI.
inclusion_criteria.quote: The main inclusion criterion was documented atrial fibrillation that occurred within 1 year be- fore screening; patients with documented atrial fibrillation that occurred more than 1 year before screening were also eligible if the participant had been receiving oral anticoagulation

criticisms.text: The trial had few secondary efficacy events and was not powered to definitively establish superiority or noninferiority for efficacy.
criticisms.quote: the num- ber of secondary efficacy end points in this study was small, and the trial was not powered to definitively establish either superiority or non- inferiority.

criticisms.text: Participants were not randomized to DAPT duration; clinician choice led to imbalances across strata and likely confounding.
criticisms.quote: Stratifi- cation to 1, 6, or 12 months of DAPT was based on clinician choice, and patients were not ran- domly assigned to a duration of DAPT.

criticisms.text: Patient characteristics were imbalanced across DAPT-duration strata and within strata across treatment groups; unidentified confounders likely differed too.
criticisms.quote: patient characteristics were imbal- anced across the strata of DAPT durations and within each stratum of DAPT durations across the three treatment groups

criticisms.text: No adjustment for multiplicity in testing multiple efficacy endpoints.
criticisms.quote: There was no adjustment for multiplicity in test- ing all these efficacy end points.

criticisms.text: Stent thrombosis was not adjudicated by a core laboratory.
criticisms.quote: Finally, stent thrombosis was not adjudicated by a core laboratory in this trial.

criticisms.text: Authors state it is inappropriate to draw firm conclusions regarding efficacy from these data.
criticisms.quote: As a result of all these limitations, it is inappropri- ate to draw firm conclusions regarding efficacy from these data.
